title: Old dog / New tricks - Advice for starting from the very basics

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
Hi Everyone
I hope you are all doing well.  Before making my first thread I wanted to respect the community here, so I read the support rules and took time to do some independent reading. After completing Driftwood Gaming's basic tutorials for MZ, I quickly learned there's an abundance of tutorials, and training resources out there, but it also feels like drinking from a firehose. The purpose of this thread is to outline my interests, goals, and vision. I'm hoping others can point me in the right direction to tutorials, plugins libraries, editors, etc., that better match these goals.
the next few sections give a bit of background about myself and the type of project i'm trying to create. If this isn't important, feel free to skip to my research section at the end which contains most of my questions.
About myself
It's been about 15 years since I seriously played around with any RPG maker, and I can immediately tell it's come a long way from Don Miguel's early work. This is a personal hobby I'm looking to pick back up, and not something I have monetary ambitions. I'm also no interested in skirting licensing or intellectual property standards. In other words, I intend to fully pay for anything I use that is not free for public use.
Engine preferences
I used a number of RPG maker engines over the years, but majority of my experience was on RPG Maker 2k3 (purchased copy). After reviewing everything out there, I've decided to use RPG Maker MZ, and have. licensed copy through Steam. I'm running off a 2025 Macbook Air, but do keep a small PC laptop nearby for things that are easier to run on windows. There are two projects I am working on, and I've listed the detailed parameters below.
Project 1 - Puzzle Game
I have a 10 month year old that is too young for video games, but one day may have interest. I'm looking to make a simple puzzle game without a battle system. I'd like to keep this game as self contained in the original RPG maker engine with minimal use of plugins or DLC. While the purpose is to give something to my daughter in the future, the project can also serve as a sandbox for learning the fundamentals of the engine without overcomplicating things.
Project 2 - Standard RPG
I have an old RPG project on RM2k3 that was never completed. I'm looking to transport that story into RMMZ. I expect it to be a tedious task, but c'est la vie. There's a few things that I am still deciding on, but the direction I take will largely depend on the options available on RMMZ.
Character design
- I'm not a fan of the chibi style generator. I find the smaller body proportion leaves little room for customization (fist pump, shrugging, etc). I found the character designs in RM2K3 much more appealing, but it's also my understanding the pixel ratio from RM2K3 to RMMZ isn't user friendly. In short, I'm looking for a character design that looks and feels like RM2k3, but not restricting other designs.
Tileset design
- Again, I am more partial to the RM2K3 designs, but not married to it. Most importantly, the style will need to look okay behind the character design.
Battle system
- I'm not opposed to the in-game battle system, as coding isn't my biggest strength. I am, however, particular about each weapon having its own animation when using attack. I understand that this is more limited in RMMZ compared to RM2k3.  Without going down a rabbit hole, I'm looking for any plugins or tutorials with a battle system closer to FFVII (original).  Each character would have its own class, weapons type, but a magic system dependent on multiple items from a specific magic equipment type.
Credit Option
- this is more of a personal preference for professionalism. I'm not sure if there's a plugin that allows you to add a Credits option at the title screen or main menu. It would simply run a common event that scrolls the names and groups who deserve recognition for any of the plugins, character designs, music, etc seen throughout the game. It would also serve as a digital bibliography as the game is being developed. (update - I found
this
)
My Research
So here's what I've collected so far from my own research. Open to any feedback or guidance the community may have. I admit in advance, that while I may try to sound like I know what I'm talking about here, I really don't. This is just how I've tried to make sense out of the enormous pile of impressive resources this community has created for each other.
RMMZ Basic Tutorials
I started with the
Driftwood Gaming basic tutorial series
of youtube videos. It was a good refresher on most things I learned on RM2k3 but provided a good primer.
If there are other basic tutorials worth a look at, i'm very much open to see it.
Advanced Tutorials
Most advance tutorials beyond the standard RMMZ engine seem to revolve around three things
i) custom assets
ii) plugins
iii) third party tools
It appears the best place for tutorials beyond the standard RMMZ engine would be the
yanfly.moe wiki page
.
Youtube is filled with numerous tutorials, but relying on the algorithm is an aimlessly wandering nightmare.
From what I can tell, each dev group on the yanfly wiki specializes on something
Ækashics Librarium = pre-made sprite assets
Caz Wolf = pre-made icon assets
Team Artrix = customizable menu plugins
VisuStella = main plugin library, generators, misc assets
Purchasing DLC
I found the following reliable places to purchase DLC both plugins and assets
Steam online shop
Yanfly.moe
RMMZ.web download section
Komodo Plaza
Is it better to get your resources from one place, or can you pick and choose?
Installing Plugins
I assume VisuStella isn't the only dev group to design plugins, but mixing the plugins between developers can cause compatibility issues?
I'm assuming the safest plugin library to use for beginners without much coding experience would be the
VisuStella MZ Tier Hierarchy System
.
Yanfly.moe provides a RMMZ specific
Troubleshooting Page
for plugin errors.
Third party tools
This is the part of my research I got a bit lost with.
These tools usually centre around customizing asset designs like tilesets and character sets.
I'm looking to learn more about third party tools that can be used to customize character sets and tilesets.
When I was using RM2k3 I would just use MS Paint to customize tiles and character, which I'm assuming is pretty rudimentary compared to tools today.
Here's what I did find on my own
The
Stella Character Generator
is quite nice, but not sure yet if it's the tool I will use.
GIMP or Asperite is a better tool to use than MS paint.
Tiled allows for more advance tileset management, but I don't think I'm willing to go that far.
I'm not really sure where I stand on all this yet. In a perfect world, I'd be able to combine the look and feel of RM2k3 assets into RMMZ, but the difference in pixel ratios seems to make this a very complicated process. The alternative is a completely different asset style that looks similar to RM2k3 but more compatible with the default pixel ratios of RMMZ.
Thank you for reading through all this. I appreciate your time and help. I apologize in advance, as I'm sure there's already one or more threads somewhere that catalogs everything I'm looking for, I simply could not find it.
I'll end this post the same way I started it. I was truly impressed to see such a strong resource sharing community for RPG makers after so many years of being away.
All the best
MDR

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I'm not quite sure, what your specific questions are (if there any hidden somewhere), or if you're just like listing your tutorial journey.
But I stumbled over the part about 2k3 and MZ resources, and how to match those in style.
RM2k3 is using a tile grid of 16x16 pixels, while MZ is using 48x48. So, infact, it's very "user friendly", as you called it, to use 2k3 chars and tiles, as you can upscale them by factor 3, to make it fit the new templates.
But in terms of style, you can't mix resolutions. A 16x16 character upscaled to 48x48 will appear to have 3 times bigger pixels.
You'll find many asset packs being 16x16 or 48x48, and also inbetweens like 32x32.
Whatever style you choose, if you upscale them, I'd highly recommend to be consistent and apply it to all your resources.
Due to the 16x16 style, 2k3 resources have a more retro vibe, while the 48x48 style allows a way more detailed style, that seems more drawing than pixel like. They shouldn't be mixed.
There are also 48x48 based Charsets in other styles than Chibi, if that's your only concern. They might be compatible with MZ RTP.

I don't use plugin collections or "multi-tool" style like the VisuStella bundle, so my approach might be somewhat different than yours. I use the RPG Maker engine as far as I hit a limitation that would affect a feature I'm working on. Eventing as much as possible. If something isn't possible with events, I'll look for a plugin or script that'll help me with this specific problem. It's an ongoing progress, and a focus on as lightweight plugins as possible, doing exactly what I need.

posts.author: MDR
posts.body: what's a memory leak?

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Usually, assets used by the game are loaded into memory for temporary use and cleared afterwards. If they aren't cleared, it's a memory leak, as there's less and less free memory available. Simple put.
HUD Maker Ultra will create clones of your entire HUD permanently without clearing them, causing notable lag or even crashes.

Update -
Hey everyone, thank-you all for your patience as I teach myself this stuff. Using a lot of your advice, I've spent the past week playing around with tilesets and pixel ratios trying to import old RM2K3 tilesets into RMMZ.
I've come to the conclusion that the best way to do this would be to use TileD for mapping instead of the RMMZ engine's mapping tool. I am by no means knowledgeable about using RMMZ, I just found it impossible to get a clean version.
If you upscale everything by 300% you have to edit the autotiles down to a 2x2 tile grid, which misaligns autotiles with detailed patterns.
If you upscale the autotiles by 200% it perfectly matches the 3x3 tile grid in MZ, but there's no way to get the rest of the tiles and character sets to match the pixel ratio.
I did find a third option. I upscale everything by 200% and realigned the remaining tiles and character sets in sheets for 48x48 pixels, but any objects with more than one tile would need a lot of custom editing.
TileD seems to provide autotile templates with a 3x3 tile grid. I'd be able to keep everything at 16x16 pixel ratio, and just switch RMMZ to 16x16. this would keep everything consistent and avoid any upscaling.
I assume others have already figured this out. Let me know if it sounds wrong, or incorrect.

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
Update -
TileD seems to have been the solution to my problem with using RM2K3 tilesets in RMMZ.
For what it's worth - I learned that the main difference between RM2K3 and RMMZ autotiles is how the side and middle tiles of a 3x3 tile grid is made. In RMMZ those tiles are simply recreated from quartered pieces of the corner tiles, while each of the 9 tiles in RM2K3 are independent. Many autotiles sets in RM2K3 have unique designs for all 9 tiles, making it impossible to reduce them to the 2x2 tile gride used in RMMZ without either losing pixel quality, or simply deleting 5 of the 9 tiles.
TileD allows me to use the full 3x3 tiles grid. The only down side is I have to manually create the terrain sets myself. VisuStella's autotile generator seems to only work with the RMMZ 2x2 tile grid.
It also took me a while to figure out how to manually add the terrain patterns

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
MDR said:
For what it's worth - I learned that the main difference between RM2K3 and RMMZ autotiles is how the side and middle tiles of a 3x3 tile grid is made. In RMMZ those tiles are simply recreated from quartered pieces of the corner tiles, while each of the 9 tiles in RM2K3 are independent. Many autotiles sets in RM2K3 have unique designs for all 9 tiles, making it impossible to reduce them to the 2x2 tile gride used in RMMZ without either losing pixel quality, or simply deleting 5 of the 9 tiles.
Click to expand...
Your numbers don't seem to quite add up here. There are, generally speaking, two ways to handle autotiles that have exactly two types of terrain: marching squares, or blob. RPGMaker has always used the blob format (at least for the full autotiles – I'm not sure what it does with waterfall, roof, and wall autotiles).
With blob, you fundamentally have 48 total variations. Most implementations drop the last variation, leaving only 47 in total. (The reason for this is that the last variation is an entirely different terrain, so it would be duplicated as the first variation in a different autotile.)
RPGMaker compresses the blob's 47 tiles into a total of 20 quarter-tiles, which are used to compose the 47 real blob tiles. Theoretically, it would be possible to reduce it to only 13 quarter-tiles, though it would look a bit repetitive. But the main point here is that there's no such thing as a "3x3 tile grid", so I'm really not sure what you're referring to when you say that.
Your images appear to be showing a full blob set of 47 tiles (plus 20 unrelated tiles beside them). I assume those images are taken from Tiled though. Are you saying that that's exactly what the Rm2k sheet looks like?
Considering that Rm2k is older than even XP, I suppose it's not too surprising to hear that they had yet to hit upon the method of compressing the autotile set into just 5 tiles. You could probably forcibly squash the tiles into that set, but it would take a lot of work. So, using Tiled might indeed be the best option for you.

replace
the RPGMaker map data file and be called Map001.json? That would also be weird though – RPGMaker would overwrite it on save, so that would really be a bad idea if you ask me. Unless it's in a separate subfolder or something.
I found
some documentation
that states the Tiled maps go in a subfolder called tmx. Did you miss that part?

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
Design Elements Menu - Explained
Took the time to outline how I'd like the Elements Menu to work. I tried to keep the battle system for this project as simple as possible, but I also know that basic level grinding is a boring system too. Magic isn't just a skill in this project, but part of the major storyline, so I'd like to give it a unique system without over complicating things.
Truthfully, I'm not expecting anyone to take the time to walk me step by step through this whole thing. I'm mainly looking to see if anyone has either design something similar or knows of someone else who designed something similar. At least then I'll know this is possible.
In total, there are four aspects of the game that need to talk to each other to make this all work (magic, equip menu, crafting menu and the elements menu).
I. Magic
This project has 7 categories of magic (fire, ice, thunder, water, earth, wind, spirit). For the purpose of this post, it's not necessary to explain "spirit" but it's where spells like light/darkness, cure, protect, etc. are based.
Magic skills are acquired one of two ways:
Leveling up the actor's class
Equip menu
The former will only apply to one actor, while the latter will apply to every other actor.
II. Equip Menu
You'll notice the equip menu is rather simple; weapon, clothing, accessory, and three sagestone slots. There are no shields in the game, and all other items like headwear, gloves, boots, etc have been rolled into accessories or clothing.
Sagestones is where magic can be equip. Without revealing too much of the story, each sagestone belongs to one of the 7 magic categories described above, i.e., equiping a fire sagestone will add a fire spell to that actor.
Most of this seems easy to do, but there's two things I've yet to work out.
1. Make multiple sagestone slots act as the same equipment type.
Bases on what I've read this can be achieved with Visustella Item and Equip core plugins. I'll look into it this after and report back.
2. Design a level up system for sagestones.
Ideally, I'd like for each sagestone to level up to strong spells (eg. FireI, FireII, FireIII). I'm not sure if VisuStella has plugins that allow for this. Perhaps a Sage Point (SP) system earned in battle that levels up each Sagestone when equiped. If this is not possible, each spell would need to be its own sagestone, which seems less exciting. I feel like there's two challenges to overcome here.
designing an SP system
designing a custom menu that shows the progress of each sagestone.
At the moment I'm exploring the VisuStella plugins for
Common Event Menu
and the
Skill Learning System
.
III. Crafting Menu
The next step is designing the crafting menu and shop, which is not meant to be too complicated. Each sagestone can be crafted with certain item(s) to add elemental effects to resistance or damage in battle. If a sagestone can be leveled up, those parameters will increase as well. I'm exploring the VisuStella Item Crafting System plugin to see if this is possible. Ironically, the first problem I'm having is actually getting into the crafting menu. This might be because I have not set up any crafting items yet.
Elements Menu
The last section is the elements menu, which I have already designed. If I can get the equip and crafting menus work properly, I'm already familiar with the elemental notetags to add to each sagestone in the RMMZ database.
The last aspect is more for aesthetics than functionality. I'd like to make these commands invisible at the beginning of the game, then added later. I'm pretty sure I can do with with variables/switches in the visustella plugins.

posts.author: MDR
posts.body:
I figured it out.
I was using 1024x1024 size tileset, simply because that's the max size VisuStella pugin instructions said RMMZ engine will allow from TileD. However the tileset size still needs to be a perfect multiple of the tile size your project is using in RMMZ.
Example: I'm using 48x48
tileset size (1024) / tile size (48) = 21.33
The fraction appears to be what screwed everything up. Once I resized the canvass size of the tileset down to 1008x1008 the objects appeared correct in both Tiled and RMMZ
1008 / 48 = 21

Removing AI Generated Content
After careful consideration, I've decided to remove the AI generated content from the project. This content was mostly Facesets and Music. I've swapped the facesets and character portraits with blank placeholders until I find a good alternative. I'd like to still use the same style, so if anyone knows of an artist who creates facesets that look similar to what I started with, I'd love to get in touch with them. For music, I'm exploring alternative options in the Pixabay library.
Credit Section
The reason for this change has a lot to do with the credit section of this project. I want to get the acknowledgement of asset contributions right. This is really a solo project, but I wouldn't say the assets used are 100% original. This lead me down the path of understanding licenses, derivatives, and the overall opinion of AI content in the indie pixel art world. Without getting into the weeds, I've concluded for myself, that the benefit of working with real artists outweighs that of using AI content for any section of the project. This isn't a statement, but a personal preference.
If anyone has any recommended artists for facesets or music I'd love to look at their work.
Thanks

License

License

License
)

Enemy Sprites => TBD. They will most likely be static images from community artists associated with the artists listed above.
I've also made it a habit to reach out to any community artist whose art I am using, give them the heads up their assets are being included.
